newsitem.title: UK: Gas mix helps drugs fight cancer, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Gas mix helps drugs fight cancer, study finds.

text.p: Inhaling a mixture of oxygen and carbon dioxide can help get anti-cancer drugs into a tumour more quickly and make them work more effectively, British doctors said on Monday.

Tumour growth virtually stopped in rats who breathed the gas mixture, John Griffiths of St George's Hospital in London told a news conference.Tests in people, not yet published, showed a similar effect.
Cancer chemotherapy relies on getting strong, toxic drugs to a tumour to kill it.

"The problem is that...on the whole cancers have very poor blood supplies," Griffiths said. But his group knew that the 95 percent oxygen and five percent carbon dioxide cocktail, known as carbogen, could increase blood flow.

They used magnetic resonance imaging and nuclear magnetic resonance to measure blood flow and drug supply in the rat tumours. Both methods are simple and do not require the use of radioactive chemicals.
When the rats breathed the gas cocktail, blood flow in and out of the tumours improved by 30 percent. "We were getting more blood into the tumours," Griffiths said.
"The host breathes it and suddenly the signal improves because we've washed out all his deoxygenated blood," Griffiths said, showing a videotape of the tumour scan.
A second scan showed that more of the drug, ifosfamide, was alos getting to the tumours. And in fact, tumour growth slowed.
"We decreased tumour growth almost completely in the first 12 days," said Griffiths, whose study is published in the January issue of the British Journal of Cancer.

Early tests on human volunteers showed that about two-thirds of tumours responded. Griffiths said he did not know why some of the tumours did not stop growing -- the ratio was the same no matter what cancer or part of the body was involved.
But he said the gas could be a cheap and effective way to improve results from chemotherapy. All the patient will have to do is breathe the gas for five to 10 minutes while undergoing chemotherapy.
